findings.title: askHuman now auto-executes, so the model answers its own question and the human-in-the-loop flow breaks.
findings.body:
The old `tool({ parameters })` had no `execute`, so generation stopped at the `askHuman` call and waited for a human to supply the tool result via `humanResponseAsToolCall`.

The new `createTool` has a `handler` that returns `question`. The SDK now produces a tool result right away: the question echoed back as the "human" answer. With multiple steps the model continues on that fake answer.

When the human later responds, `humanResponseAsToolCall` saves a second `tool-result` for the same `toolCallId`. The thread then holds duplicate or conflicting results.

Fix: keep this as a tool with no execute. Use `tool({ description, inputSchema: z.object(...) })` from "ai", with no `execute`.

findings.title: Chat model is retyped as `LanguageModelV1` and forced with `as any`, contrary to the v5 migration and the 'remove type assertions' goal.
findings.body:
AI SDK v5 providers return `LanguageModelV2`. The change downgrades the declared type to `LanguageModelV1` and then casts `openai.languageModel(...) as any` to make it compile.

That in turn forces `chat: chat as any` in every agent (fashion, simple, story, weather, addFile, rateLimiting, agentAsTool) and `as any` in threads.ts and the rag files. The PR states it removes all `as any` assertions; it adds them throughout and hides real type mismatches.

Fix: keep `LanguageModelV2`, remove the casts, and fix any genuine incompatibilities they hide.

findings.title: Tool result `output` is a raw string hidden behind `as any`, not the v5 output shape.
findings.body:
In AI SDK v5, a `tool-result` part's `output` must be a typed object such as `{ type: "text", value: string }`. Passing the bare `args.response` string and casting with `as any` silences the type error but stores an invalid part.

Saving it, or later converting it back into model messages, will either fail validation or send malformed tool results to the provider.

Fix: use `output: { type: "text", value: args.response }` and drop the cast.

findings.title: The `ai` peer dependency range is widened to unbounded `>=5.0.0-beta.29`.
findings.body:
`>=` accepts any future major version (ai v6, v7, ...), which this library has not been built or tested against. Installs with breaking majors would be allowed silently.

The example-directory fix does not call for changing the published peer range.

Fix: restore `^5.0.0-beta.29` or use `^5.0.0`.

findings.title: MockLanguageModelV2 is fed V1-shaped responses, so tests don't exercise real behaviour.
findings.body:
The mock is now `MockLanguageModelV2`, but `doGenerate` and `doStream` still return V1 shapes:
- `text` instead of a `content` array
- `textDelta` instead of `delta`
- usage with `promptTokens`/`completionTokens` instead of `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`
- `defaultObjectGenerationMode` and `logprobs`

Under V2 the generated text is empty and usage is undefined, so assertions on output either fail or silently test nothing.

Also, `LanguageModelV2` and `LanguageModelV2StreamPart` are exported from `@ai-sdk/provider`, not "ai".

Fix: update the mock results to the V2 shapes.

findings.title: Tool call input is still read through a type assertion, not checked at runtime.
findings.body:
The PR says `(input as { question: string }).question` was replaced with runtime type checking, but this line is exactly that cast.

If the input is malformed, `question` is `undefined` and flows on unchecked.

Fix: validate it, e.g. `z.object({ question: z.string() }).parse(tc.input)`.

held.title: Renaming the public action arg `mimeType` to `mediaType` breaks clients that still send `mimeType`.
held.body:
`uploadFile` and `askAboutImage` (autoSave.ts) are public actions. Convex argument validation rejects calls that pass `mimeType` or omit `mediaType`.

Any frontend code calling these with the old field will start failing. I could not see whether the example UI was updated in this PR.

held.title: Usage mapping reads `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`, which may not exist on the usage passed in.
held.body:
`vUsage` and the internal schema still use `promptTokens`/`completionTokens`. If the `UsageHandler` receives the internal `Usage` shape, then `args.usage.inputTokens` and `args.usage.outputTokens` are `undefined`. The `|| 0` fallback then records 0 prompt and completion tokens for every call, silently corrupting billing data.

I could not see the `UsageHandler` type or where it is called, so I could not confirm which shape it gets. Verify the type, and drop the `|| 0` defaults so a mismatch fails loudly instead of recording zeros.

held.title: Removing `NoInfer` from `stopWhen` lets it influence inference of `AgentTools`.
held.body:
`NoInfer` kept `stopWhen` from driving inference of the agent's tool type. Without it, a `stopWhen` condition typed for other tools can widen or alter the inferred `AgentTools`, weakening type checks for library users.

This public-API typing change is outside the example-directory fix. If `NoInfer` is unavailable in some TypeScript version, prefer a local `NoInfer` helper.
